On June 4, 1920, Hungary signed a treaty that erased 72% of its own country.

This map redraws that exact scale of loss onto the United States — so you can actually feel what it looked like.

a thread 🧵🗺️

1/ The real Treaty of Trianon: Hungary went from 325,000 km² to 93,000 km². Population fell from 20.9 million to 7.6 million.

Roughly 3 million ethnic Hungarians woke up living in someone else's country — without moving an inch.

2/ Where did it go? Romania got Transylvania, the single biggest slice. Czechoslovakia took Slovakia and Ruthenia. The new Yugoslavia absorbed Croatia-Slavonia and Vojvodina. Austria got a strip called Burgenland.

3/ Now scale that onto the US map: Japan holds the West Coast, the UK takes the Midwest and Northeast, Spain and Mexico split the South, and what's left of America is a landlocked strip in the middle.
4/ That's the real shock of Trianon — it wasn't just land, it was the coastline. Hungary lost its only seaport at Fiume and became fully landlocked, just like the shrunken 'USA' in this map.
5/ Hungary never fully accepted it. "Nem, nem, soha!" — "No, no, never!" — became the interwar slogan, and Trianon still shapes Hungarian politics and border debates today, over a century later.

6/ A single signature in a French palace can do more damage than most wars. Trianon is the sharpest reminder of that in modern history.

What other treaty should we map like this? Follow @forummapping and tell us.
